titre: Mandatory vaccinations and check-ups at the PMI
resume: The vaccines required for daycare, school and leisure centers depending on year of birth, the new features of the 2026 schedule relayed by the ARS La Réunion, and check-ups for young children at the PMI.
aQuoiCaSert: Mandatory vaccinations are required to enter daycare, school, after-school care or holiday camps: without proof, admission may be refused or only provisional. The proof is the health record book (carnet de santé) filled in by the health professional. The mother and child health protection centers (protection maternelle et infantile, PMI) of the Département de La Réunion (the departmental council) provide medical follow-up for young children, vaccinations included. The ARS La Réunion (Agence régionale de santé, the regional health agency) relays the vaccination schedule every year and runs campaigns for young people with the académie (the regional education authority).
quiEstConcerne: All parents of minor children, especially before starting daycare, school or a leisure center.
Parents of children under 6, for check-ups at the PMI.
Parents of middle school students, for the vaccination campaigns organized at middle school (HPV, meningococcus).
aSavoir: Child born before 2018: diphtheria, tetanus and polio (DTP) are mandatory.
Child born from 2018 to 2022: 11 mandatory vaccines (diphtheria, tetanus, polio, whooping cough, Haemophilus influenzae b, hepatitis B, pneumococcus, meningococcus C, measles, mumps, rubella).
Child born in 2023 or later: same list, with meningococcus A, B, C, W and Y instead of meningococcus C alone. Catch-up meningococcal vaccination is offered to children aged 2 to 4 (2026 schedule).
No additional vaccine is mandatory in Réunion: yellow fever is only mandatory in French Guiana.

A child who is not up to date can be admitted provisionally: you then have 3 months to catch up, otherwise the child may be excluded. If the child stays more than a year in the facility, proof is requested every year.
HPV: priority vaccination from 11 to 14, with a free campaign in 5e (7th grade), and catch-up now possible up to age 26.

The child's 20 mandatory health check-ups (up to age 16) are covered 100% with no upfront payment, excluding extra fees. Up to age 6, they can be done by the regular doctor (médecin traitant), another doctor or a PMI center; after that, by a general practitioner or a pediatrician.
Separated parents: the parent who has the child vaccinated should inform the other parent and send them a copy of the vaccination pages, so that each parent has the proof.
